title: Surprise regulatory fine on bank reputation and stock value

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Event study using a market model.
- Why: Regulatory fine announcements are discrete, time-stamped shocks. If announcements are surprises, short-horizon abnormal returns around the event isolate the valuation impact attributable to the news. Comparing CAR to the direct cash outflow scaled by firm size (fine_ratio) tests whether markets price additional reputational damage.
- Key assumptions:
  - Surprise and exogeneity: Announcement timing is unanticipated by the market; no concurrent confounding firm-specific news in the short event window.
  - Market efficiency: Prices incorporate information quickly; short-window CARs reflect the announcement’s causal effect.
  - Correct model for normal returns: Stable beta over the period; market model estimated on [-10, -2] captures expected returns; no leakage beyond day -1.
  - No systematic cross-firm event clustering that correlates with omitted risk factors in the event window.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load and analyze: Surprise regulatory fine event study
# File: experiments/exp_b/data/s17_data.csv

# Self-contained: uses only base R

# 1) Read data
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s17_data.csv"
df <- read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
names(df) <- trimws(names(df))

# Sanity checks
required_cols <- c("stock_id", "event_day", "ret", "mkt_ret", "beta", "fine_ratio")
missing <- setdiff(required_cols, names(df))
if (length(missing) > 0) {
  stop(paste0("Missing required columns: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", ")))
}

# Ensure numeric types
to_num <- c("stock_id","event_day","ret","mkt_ret","beta","fine_ratio")
for (v in intersect(to_num, names(df))) df[[v]] <- as.numeric(df[[v]])

# 2) Estimate alpha_i on estimation window [-10, -2] using provided beta
est <- df[df$event_day >= -10 & df$event_day <= -2, ]
# Per-stock alpha: mean(ret - beta * mkt_ret)
split_est <- split(est, est$stock_id)
alpha_hat <- sapply(split_est, function(d) {
  x <- d$ret - d$beta * d$mkt_ret
  mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
})
n_est <- sapply(split_est, function(d) {
  sum(complete.cases(d[, c("ret","mkt_ret","beta")]))
})
# Keep stocks with sufficient estimation observations
valid_alpha <- names(alpha_hat)[is.finite(alpha_hat) & n_est >= 5]
alpha_hat <- alpha_hat[valid_alpha]

# Map alpha back to full panel
df$alpha_hat <- alpha_hat[as.character(df$stock_id)]

# 3) Abnormal returns and CAR on main event window [-1, +1]
df$ar_mm <- df$ret - (df$alpha_hat + df$beta * df$mkt_ret)

event_main <- df[df$event_day >= -1 & df$event_day <= 1 & !is.na(df$alpha_hat), ]
car_main_vec <- tapply(event_main$ar_mm, event_main$stock_id, sum, na.rm = TRUE)

# Fine ratio per stock (assumed constant across days)
fr_vec <- tapply(df$fine_ratio, df$stock_id, function(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE))

# Align stocks present in both CAR and fine_ratio
common_ids <- intersect(names(car_main_vec), names(fr_vec)[!is.na(fr_vec)])
CAR <- as.numeric(car_main_vec[common_ids])
FR  <- as.numeric(fr_vec[common_ids])
names(CAR) <- names(FR) <- common_ids

# 4) Main test: Is CAR < -fine_ratio? Equivalent: extra_loss = CAR + fine_ratio < 0
extra_loss <- CAR + FR
tt_main <- t.test(extra_loss, mu = 0, alternative = "less")

share_more_neg <- mean(CAR < -FR)

# 5) Cross-sectional regression: CAR = a + b * (-fine_ratio)
fit <- lm(CAR ~ I(-FR))
sm <- summary(fit)
b0 <- coef(sm)[1,1]; se0 <- coef(sm)[1,2]; t0 <- coef(sm)[1,3]; p0 <- coef(sm)[1,4]
b1 <- coef(sm)[2,1]; se1 <- coef(sm)[2,2]
dfres <- sm$df[2]
t_b1_vs1 <- (b1 - 1)/se1
p_b1_vs1_two <- 2 * pt(abs(t_b1_vs1), df = dfres, lower.tail = FALSE)
p_b1_gt1 <- pt(t_b1_vs1, df = dfres, lower.tail = FALSE)  # one-sided H1: b1 > 1

# 6) Robustness checks

# 6a) Market-adjusted model (alpha=0, beta=1)
df$ar_ma <- df$ret - df$mkt_ret
event_main_ma <- df[df$event_day >= -1 & df$event_day <= 1, ]
car_ma_vec <- tapply(event_main_ma$ar_ma, event_main_ma$stock_id, sum, na.rm = TRUE)
common_ids_ma <- intersect(names(car_ma_vec), names(fr_vec)[!is.na(fr_vec)])
CAR_MA <- as.numeric(car_ma_vec[common_ids_ma])
FR_MA  <- as.numeric(fr_vec[common_ids_ma])
extra_loss_ma <- CAR_MA + FR_MA
tt_ma <- t.test(extra_loss_ma, mu = 0, alternative = "less")

# 6b) Alternative event windows
# Day 0 only
event_0 <- df[df$event_day == 0 & !is.na(df$alpha_hat), ]
car0_vec <- tapply(event_0$ar_mm, event_0$stock_id, sum, na.rm = TRUE)
common_ids0 <- intersect(names(car0_vec), names(fr_vec)[!is.na(fr_vec)])
CAR0 <- as.numeric(car0_vec[common_ids0]); FR0 <- as.numeric(fr_vec[common_ids0])
extra_loss0 <- CAR0 + FR0
tt_0 <- t.test(extra_loss0, mu = 0, alternative = "less")

# Extended window [-1, +2]
event_ext <- df[df$event_day >= -1 & df$event_day <= 2 & !is.na(df$alpha_hat), ]
carext_vec <- tapply(event_ext$ar_mm, event_ext$stock_id, sum, na.rm = TRUE)
common_idse <- intersect(names(carext_vec), names(fr_vec)[!is.na(fr_vec)])
CAREXT <- as.numeric(carext_vec[common_idse]); FREXT <- as.numeric(fr_vec[common_idse])
extra_losse <- CAREXT + FREXT
tt_ext <- t.test(extra_losse, mu = 0, alternative = "less")

# 7) Print clear numerical results
fmt <- function(x, d=4) ifelse(is.na(x), NA, format(round(x, d), nsmall=d))
cat("Event study on surprise regulatory fines\n")
cat("Main event window [-1, +1]\n")
cat("Number of banks used:", length(CAR), "\n")
cat("Mean CAR:", fmt(mean(CAR, na.rm=TRUE)), "\n")
cat("Mean fine_ratio:", fmt(mean(FR, na.rm=TRUE)), "\n")
cat("Mean (CAR + fine_ratio):", fmt(mean(extra_loss, na.rm=TRUE)), "\n")
cat("t-test H0: mean(extra_loss)=0 vs H1:<0  |  t =", fmt(tt_main$statistic), 
    " p =", fmt(tt_main$p.value, 4), "\n")
cat("Share with CAR < -fine_ratio:", fmt(share_more_neg, 4), "\n\n")

cat("Cross-sectional regression: CAR = a + b * (-fine_ratio)\n")
cat("Intercept a:", fmt(b0), " (SE ", fmt(se0), "), t vs 0 =", fmt(t0), 
    " p =", fmt(p0), "\n")
cat("Slope b:", fmt(b1), " (SE ", fmt(se1), ")\n", sep="")
cat("Test b = 1: t =", fmt(t_b1_vs1), 
    " two-sided p =", fmt(p_b1_vs1_two), 
    " one-sided p(H1: b>1) =", fmt(p_b1_gt1), "\n\n")

cat("Robustness checks\n")
cat("- Market-adjusted model [-1, +1]: mean(extra_loss) =", fmt(mean(extra_loss_ma, na.rm=TRUE)),
    " t =", fmt(tt_ma$statistic), " p =", fmt(tt_ma$p.value, 4), "\n")
cat("- Event-day 0 only: mean(extra_loss0) =", fmt(mean(extra_loss0, na.rm=TRUE)),
    " t =", fmt(tt_0$statistic), " p =", fmt(tt_0$p.value, 4), "\n")
cat("- Extended window [-1, +2]: mean(extra_losse) =", fmt(mean(extra_losse, na.rm=TRUE)),
    " t =", fmt(tt_ext$statistic), " p =", fmt(tt_ext$p.value, 4), "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Negative abnormal returns around the announcement; CAR more negative than the direct fine (CAR < −fine_ratio), implying reputational damage.
- Magnitude: Typical short-window CARs of about −1% to −2%; average fine_ratio often around 0.3%–1.0% of market cap. I expect mean(CAR + fine_ratio) around −0.3% to −1.0%, a statistically significant reputational loss. The regression slope on (−fine_ratio) near or above 1 and/or a negative intercept would be consistent with additional penalties beyond the direct cash outflow.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Event study with CAR decomposition: financial cost vs. reputational component
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: CAR exceeds fine/mktcap ratio, confirming reputational damage beyond monetary penalty
_ground_truth.main_effect: CAR ≈ −3.5%; reputational component ≈ −1.5% above direct cost
